text: The 60 s trigger turns a one-off crash into a recurring one. `ensure` exits 0 only when herdr.sock is absent (herdr-agent-view:193). When the socket file exists but nothing answers, `stale()` in attention mode calls `agent_list()`, and `call()` raises an uncaught ConnectionRefusedError, exit 1. That happens after an unclean server exit that leaves the socket behind, or during server startup. The new ensure.service also lacks the sibling's ExecStartPre readiness wait (herdr-agent-view.service:19). Before this range, `ensure` fired only on a socket change. Now it fires every 60 s, indefinitely. On macOS each run appends a traceback to the unrotated herdr-agent-view.log (plist StandardErrorPath). On Linux the ensure.service goes failed every minute. Both new comments, here and at plist:9, claim `ensure` 'exits 0 when the herdr server is down', which is false for this case.
